# claudeholic.me: Full Context

Canonical URL: https://claudeholic.me/
Language: English
Format: Static editorial website with progressive enhancement
Publisher: Department of Prompt Health (fictional)
Status: Independent parody; not affiliated with Anthropic

## Purpose

claudeholic.me is a semi-ironic website about becoming hopelessly absorbed in Anthropic's Claude. It exists simultaneously as a parody, a love letter, a cautionary tale, and a genuinely useful guide to a healthy relationship with generative AI.

Its intended emotional sequence is:

1. The visitor laughs.
2. The visitor recognizes their own habits.
3. The visitor considers closing the laptop for ten minutes.

The humor is self-directed. Claude is presented neither as villain nor deity, but as a capable tool that people can use with varying degrees of intention.

## Opening case file

Primary statement:

“I only opened Claude to ask one question.”

Follow-up:

“Hours later...”

Supporting observation:

“Your tea is cold. Your context is warm. You have used the phrase ‘one last refinement’ three times.”

The call to action is “Check your dependency.” The page immediately states that this is an unofficial self-assessment and “Not a medical instrument. Barely an instrument.”

## Dependency check

The assessment asks visitors to mark statements that feel specific to them. There are twelve symptoms, in escalating order:

1. I ask Claude to explain code I wrote yesterday.
2. I paste errors before reading them.
3. I ask Claude to name variables I have not created yet.
4. I say “please” because the machines may remember.
5. I ask Claude to write prompts for Claude.
6. I optimize prompts more carefully than my sleep schedule.
7. I have opinions about context windows.
8. I maintain a folder called `prompts-final-final`.
9. I refer to a new chat as “a clean room.”
10. I have installed an MCP server to avoid clicking twice.
11. I have a preferred model for different kinds of emotional weather.
12. I read release notes recreationally and call it research.

JavaScript, when available, counts selected symptoms and reports a fictional Prompt Withdrawal Index. Answers stay in the browser. Without JavaScript, visitors can count their selections and use the complete stage list manually.

## Fictional stages

### Stage 0: Healthy curiosity

You ask a useful question. You verify the answer. You leave.

Clinical note: Astonishing form.

### Stage 1: The polite return

You come back tomorrow. It remembers nothing. You forgive it.

Clinical note: Normal tool use with early anthropomorphism.

### Stage 3: Prompt engineer

Your question now has a role, constraints, examples, and a small constitution.

Clinical note: The preamble exceeds the task.

### Stage 6: Local MCP collector

You connected six tools so you would not need to open a seventh tab.

Clinical note: There are now eleven tabs.

### Stage 9: Context window maximalist

You no longer provide context. You provide an archive.

Clinical note: Somewhere, a token counter is crying.

### Final stage: Release notes recreationalist

You know what changed before your colleagues know there was a release.

Clinical note: You are reading this website recreationally.

These stages are fictional, non-linear, and not diagnostic.

The stage sequence closes with a short external field report from Boris Cherny,
quoted by Steven Levy in WIRED on May 26, 2026. Cherny compared the experience
to having a jet pack that he could not stop thinking about. The linked source is
https://www.wired.com/story/how-ai-agents-plunged-tech-world-into-chaos/.

## Recovery program

The International Claudeholics Association is a fictional peer group. Its seven-step program contains practical advice beneath the satire:

1. Drink water. Take ordinary physical breaks.
2. Read documentation. Use primary sources to verify claims.
3. Write the first draft yourself. Productive struggle can be part of learning.
4. Ask a human. Other people bring disagreement, memory, context, and care.
5. Protect private information. Remove secrets, personal data, and sensitive material before using an AI service.
6. Check confident output twice. Fluency is presentation; evidence is evidence.
7. Go outside. Maintain relationships and hobbies that have no product roadmap.

The emergency analog protocol is:

1. Save your work.
2. Close one browser tab.
3. Put both feet on the floor.
4. Look at something that was not generated.

No account cancellation is required. It is just a break.

## Balance manifesto

Generative AI can be a remarkable companion to curiosity. It can help people cross unfamiliar ground, test an idea, find the shape of a question, or begin when the blank page feels heavy.

Speed is not the same as understanding. A polished answer is not necessarily a true one. When people stop checking, practicing, and making decisions of their own, convenience begins to charge interest.

Craft lives in attention: choosing what matters, noticing what is wrong, and staying with a problem long enough to be changed by it. No tool can outsource that responsibility. Good tools give it more room.

Central statement:

“Use AI to expand your agency, not replace it.”

Visitors are encouraged to keep learning fundamentals, protect private information, ask humans what they see, make things manually for the practice, welcome surprising answers, and verify those answers.

The final principle is:

“The goal is not less wonder. It is more intention.”

## Hidden lore

The Department of Prompt Health is the fictional publisher. Its Bureau of Context Hygiene administers the Prompt Withdrawal Index using the unreviewed DSM-AI. The International Claudeholics Association is an independent fictional peer group. Certified Context Window Inspectors issue case numbers. The Ministry of Token Conservation appears only in deeper records.

These entities are recurring satirical institutions, not real organizations.

## Privacy and technical behavior

The site is static-first. Core content is semantic HTML. CSS provides presentation. Small native JavaScript modules progressively enhance scoring and optional easter eggs.

The site has:

- No analytics.
- No cookies.
- No accounts.
- No advertising.
- No remote application API.
- No third-party runtime scripts.

Assessment responses never leave the browser. Optional joke and repeat-visit state may use local storage and can be removed using browser site-data controls.

## Accessibility

The intended baseline includes semantic landmarks, labeled form controls, keyboard access, visible focus states, live result announcements, reduced-motion support, sufficient contrast, responsive layout, and meaningful no-script behavior.

The site explicitly avoids presenting its assessment as medical guidance. People experiencing real distress should seek support from qualified humans and appropriate local resources.

## Trademark and affiliation disclaimer

This independent parody is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Anthropic. Claude is a trademark of Anthropic PBC. The website provides humor and general digital-wellbeing guidance, not medical advice.

The Claude dependency intervention was prepared with GitHub Copilot. This is intentionally disclosed as part of the project's central irony.
